title: Banks need 'bare metal' recovery in face of AI risks, says BoE's Breeden
key_facts: Breeden said the Bank is working with banks on deep cyber-recovery options
She said it is no longer enough to assume attackers won't get through
She told the IIF annual meeting in Bangkok that AI poses a 'systemic risk' to the global financial system
Bare metal systems are entirely independent of a bank's main tech and kick in if primary systems are compromised
The Bank is surveying banks on readiness for quantum computing risks to encryption
The IMF warned Tuesday an AI-enabled cyberattack on a critical service could undermine confidence
Concern: hackers or hostile states weaponising advanced AI models, and rogue AI agents
quote_evidence: "It's not enough now to assume that the cyber attackers won't get through," Breeden said.
"The thing that I worry about the most is waking up and one of our most systemically important banks or a bit of core infrastructure has been attacked and is paralysed," she said.
why_it_matters_hint: A major regulator is moving banks toward AI-era recovery planning.
